pages.title: High openness: exploring widely and choosing deliberately
pages.summary: A high openness result suggests frequent engagement with ideas, imagination, aesthetics, feelings, varied actions, or reconsidered assumptions; it does not rank intelligence or creativity.
pages.meaning: This range points to a relatively strong tendency to notice possibilities and engage with unfamiliar or conceptually rich material. The expression can differ across the six facets, so a broad result does not require equal interest in art, abstract debate, emotional exploration, novelty, or changing conventions.
pages.possible_patterns: You may generate several interpretations before settling on one, connect information across fields, or stay engaged when a task leaves room for experimentation. In routine work, you may improve the process by questioning assumptions, but you may also keep alternatives open after the decision value has started to fall.
pages.counterexample: Someone in this range can prefer a familiar breakfast, use detailed procedures, or reject a fashionable idea after examining it. High openness concerns a recurring orientation toward experience and thought, not constant novelty seeking or opposition to every convention.
pages.context_variation: Exploration may become more visible when time, psychological safety, and reversible choices are available. Under fatigue, deadline pressure, financial constraint, or a high-consequence decision, the same person may narrow options and rely on established methods without changing the underlying result.
pages.combination_effects: With higher conscientiousness, exploration may be converted into prototypes, criteria, and follow-through; with lower conscientiousness, idea generation may outpace closure. Higher extraversion can make exploration collaborative and verbal, while lower extraversion may keep it private, research-heavy, or reflective.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include reframing a stale problem, tolerating conceptual ambiguity, and discovering non-obvious connections. Tradeoffs can include diffusion of attention, repeated restarts, or undervaluing the coordination benefit of a stable standard. Neither side is automatic, and the useful balance depends on the task.
pages.communication_action: For one live decision, list no more than three genuinely different options, define the evidence that would change your choice, and set a stopping time. Tell collaborators which parts remain exploratory and which parts are already committed so curiosity does not create avoidable uncertainty.
pages.not_meaning: This result does not mean smarter, more cultured, more creative, morally better, unable to follow rules, suited to every innovative job, or destined to dislike routine. It is not a diagnosis, an ability test, a hiring criterion, or a prediction of achievement.
pages.method_boundary: Range labels summarize a continuous self-report result and can hide facet differences, response conditions, and situational constraints. Interpret repeated examples and counterexamples over time; do not treat the label as a fixed identity or infer individual validity from group-level research.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports a named hierarchical trait model, not the accuracy of an individual FermatMind range result.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Reports group-level patterns across studies; it does not predict how or whether one person's result will change.

pages.title: 开放性较高：扩大探索，也给选择设置停止条件
pages.summary: 开放性较高表示更常接近观念、想象、审美、感受、多样行动或对既有假设的复查，但不代表智力、创意或见识等级。
pages.meaning: 这个区间提示你较常留意可能性，也较愿意进入陌生、复杂或需要重新解释的材料。六个侧面的强弱可能并不整齐，所以总分较高不要求你同时热爱艺术、抽象讨论、情绪探索、新活动和挑战惯例。
pages.possible_patterns: 面对含糊任务时，你可能先提出多种解释，把不同领域的信息连接起来，或通过试做发现原问题问错了。代价也可能出现在选项越开越多、执行阶段重新起题，以及把本应共享的稳定规则过早改掉。
pages.counterexample: 开放性较高的人仍可坚持固定作息、认真使用清单，也可能在核对成本后拒绝一个看似新潮的方案。这个结果描述的是较常出现的取向，不是要求每件事都创新或反对传统。
pages.context_variation: 当时间充足、试错可撤回、团队允许提出不同看法时，探索通常更明显；在睡眠不足、期限迫近、资源紧张或后果很高时，同一个人也可能主动缩小选项并采用成熟流程。
pages.combination_effects: 与较高尽责性组合时，点子更可能被转成标准、原型和交付节点；与较低尽责性组合时，生成速度可能超过收束速度。较高外向性会让探索更多发生在对话中，较低外向性则可能表现为独自阅读、写作和长时间推演。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是重构旧问题、容纳暂时的不确定，以及发现不容易被看见的联系；潜在代价是注意力分散、频繁重启，或低估统一做法对协作的价值。哪一边更重要取决于任务后果与团队需求。
pages.communication_action: 选一个正在进行的决策，只保留三个真正不同的方案，写明什么新证据会改变选择，并设置停止搜索的时间。同步告诉协作者哪些部分仍可讨论、哪些部分已经锁定，避免好奇心制造额外不确定。
pages.not_meaning: 它不代表更聪明、更有文化、更有创造力、更善良，也不代表无法遵守规则、适合所有创新岗位或注定厌恶重复。它不是医疗诊断、能力测试、招聘标准或成就预测。
pages.method_boundary: 区间标签压缩了连续自评结果，也可能遮住六个侧面的差异、作答状态与现实约束。解释时要寻找跨情境的重复例子和反例，不能把群体研究直接当成个人准确性或固定身份的证明。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持一个明确命名的层级特质模型，不证明个人费马测试区间结果准确。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 报告跨研究的群体变化模式，不能预测某个个人是否或如何变化。

pages.title: Middle openness: changing the exploration threshold by context
pages.summary: A middle openness result is a selective pattern, not an absence of personality: you may explore when the expected value clears a context-dependent threshold and preserve familiar methods elsewhere.
pages.meaning: This range suggests that exploration and continuity are both available strategies. The deciding threshold may shift with the topic, consequence, familiarity, time budget, and reversibility. A middle result can also combine stronger and weaker facets rather than placing every facet near the center.
pages.possible_patterns: You may seek alternatives for an important design problem but use a proven workflow for administration, enjoy new concepts inside a familiar field, or experiment only after the baseline is understood. Others may experience you as inventive in one setting and conventional in another because the decision rules changed.
pages.counterexample: Trying one unusual hobby does not establish high openness, and declining a risky change does not establish low openness. A middle-range person can make a bold conceptual move when evidence is strong or stay with routine when novelty would add coordination cost without improving the result.
pages.context_variation: Low-stakes trials, trusted collaborators, and adequate preparation may lower the threshold for exploration. Public scrutiny, unclear ownership, irreversible consequences, or overload may raise it. The useful observation is which conditions change the threshold, not whether behavior looks consistent in every scene.
pages.combination_effects: Higher conscientiousness may turn selective exploration into planned pilots with explicit review points; lower conscientiousness may make the threshold depend more on immediate interest. Higher neuroticism can raise the evidence needed for uncertain changes, while lower neuroticism may make reversible trials easier to start.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include matching novelty to consequence, translating between exploratory and stability-oriented teammates, and avoiding change for its own sake. Tradeoffs can include appearing inconsistent, delaying a clear position, or using context as an excuse when the actual decision rule has never been stated.
pages.communication_action: Before the next proposal, write a two-column rule: conditions that justify exploring and conditions that justify keeping the baseline. Share the rule, run one reversible test, and review whether the threshold matched the actual stakes instead of defending the outcome after it happens.
pages.not_meaning: Middle does not mean average in ability, indecisive, bland, balanced in every facet, or without a recognizable pattern. It does not guarantee flexibility, and it should not be converted into a type, diagnosis, hiring judgment, or prediction of future performance.
pages.method_boundary: A cut label cannot show the exact score, uncertainty, facet profile, or context behind a response. Use it to investigate thresholds and repeated choices, not to claim a stable midpoint across all domains of life or to infer personal change from group-level evidence.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports hierarchical trait measurement, not a universal meaning for every middle-range score.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Group-level change evidence does not establish individual score movement or explain one context shift.

pages.title: 开放性中间区间：根据情境调整探索门槛
pages.summary: 中间区间具有明确的选择性模式：当新方案的预期价值超过情境门槛时扩大选项，在其他任务中保留熟悉做法。
pages.meaning: 这个区间说明探索与延续都可能成为你的可用策略，选择哪一个会受主题、后果、熟悉度、时间预算和可撤回程度影响。它也可能来自六个侧面一高一低的组合，而不是每个侧面都正好居中。
pages.possible_patterns: 你可能在重要的产品问题上主动寻找替代解释，却在行政流程中沿用成熟步骤；也可能愿意进入熟悉领域的新理论，但会先理解基线再改变实际做法。旁人因此可能在不同场景给出相反印象。
pages.counterexample: 尝试一次陌生活动不能证明开放性很高，拒绝一次高风险变更也不能证明开放性很低。中间区间的人可以在证据充分时做大胆调整，也可以在新意只会增加协作成本时坚持原方案。
pages.context_variation: 低成本试验、可信的协作者和充分准备会降低探索门槛；公开评价、责任不清、不可逆后果或信息过载会提高门槛。需要观察的不是每个情境都一致，而是什么条件在推动门槛移动。
pages.combination_effects: 与较高尽责性组合时，有选择的探索可能变成带评审点的计划试验；与较低尽责性组合时，是否探索可能更依赖当下兴趣。较高神经质可能提高不确定变更所需的证据，较低神经质则可能更快启动可撤回的小测试。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是让新意匹配后果、在探索型与稳定型成员之间翻译需求，并减少为了变化而变化；潜在代价是看起来前后不一、迟迟不表态，或用“看情况”掩盖从未说清的判断规则。
pages.communication_action: 面对下一项提议，先写两列条件：哪些情况值得探索，哪些情况应该保留基线。把规则公开，运行一个可撤回测试，再复盘门槛是否匹配真实后果，而不是事后为结果找理由。
pages.not_meaning: 中间区间不代表能力普通、优柔寡断、性格平淡、六个侧面都平衡，也不自动保证灵活。它不能被换算成人格类型、医疗诊断、招聘判断或未来绩效预测。
pages.method_boundary: 区间切分无法显示精确分数、不确定性、侧面组合和作答背景。它适合帮助你调查门槛与重复选择，不适合宣称所有生活领域都稳定居中，也不能用群体变化研究解释一次情境波动。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持层级特质测量，不代表所有中间区间分数都有同一种含义。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 群体变化证据不能证明个人分数移动，也不能解释一次情境差异。

pages.title: Low openness: using stable methods and testing change by evidence
pages.summary: A low openness result suggests a stronger preference for familiar, concrete, or proven approaches in many situations; it does not mean unintelligent, unimaginative, or incapable of change.
pages.meaning: This range points to a relatively strong tendency to value continuity, practical evidence, and approaches whose costs are already understood. Expression can vary by facet: a person may prefer familiar routines while still responding deeply to art, questioning a convention, or exploring ideas inside a trusted field.
pages.possible_patterns: You may ask for a concrete example before adopting an abstract proposal, improve reliability by preserving a known process, or learn best when new material connects to an existing application. When change arrives without evidence or ownership, you may focus first on disruption, training cost, and what the old method already solves.
pages.counterexample: A person in this range can invent a practical workaround, enjoy fiction, travel somewhere unfamiliar, or lead a major change after the case is proven. Preferring tested methods is not the same as lacking curiosity, imagination, courage, or capacity to learn.
pages.context_variation: Openness may become more visible when a new option solves a concrete recurring problem, a trusted person demonstrates it, or the first trial is reversible. It may become less visible when terminology is abstract, implementation cost is hidden, or change threatens a reliable system without a clear benefit.
pages.combination_effects: With higher conscientiousness, this range may support careful standardization and dependable execution; with lower conscientiousness, familiar choices may be preserved without consistent maintenance. Higher agreeableness can make change concerns quieter and cooperative, while lower agreeableness may make objections more direct and evidence-focused.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include protecting continuity, noticing implementation cost, and turning broad proposals into concrete requirements. Tradeoffs can include discounting an unfamiliar idea too early, overvaluing past success, or waiting for certainty that the decision cannot provide. The appropriate balance depends on reversibility and consequence.
pages.communication_action: When a new method is proposed, ask for the baseline problem, one observable success measure, the switching cost, and a rollback point. Agree to a bounded trial when those items are clear; this preserves useful caution without requiring either immediate adoption or permanent refusal.
pages.not_meaning: This result does not mean less intelligent, less creative, narrow-minded, morally worse, unable to learn, opposed to all change, or suited only to routine work. It is not a diagnosis, ability judgment, hiring filter, or forecast of achievement.
pages.method_boundary: A range label compresses a continuous self-report score and may obscure facet-specific curiosity, cultural expectations, access to novelty, and current stress. Interpret the pattern through repeated choices and counterexamples rather than treating the label as a fixed limitation.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports a hierarchical trait model, not deficit language or a personal ability conclusion.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Group-level change patterns do not promise change or stability for one individual.

pages.title: 开放性较低：保护稳定，也用证据决定何时改变
pages.summary: 开放性较低表示在许多情境中更偏好熟悉、具体或经过验证的做法，但不代表智力低、没有想象力或无法改变。
pages.meaning: 这个区间提示你较重视连续性、实际证据和成本已经比较清楚的做法。六个侧面仍可能不同：一个人可以偏好固定日程，同时被艺术打动、检视某项惯例，或在熟悉领域持续钻研新观念。
pages.possible_patterns: 面对抽象提议时，你可能先要求具体例子；在协作中，你可能通过保留成熟流程提高可靠性；学习新材料时，你也可能需要先连接实际用途。当变更缺少证据和负责人时，你会优先看到中断、训练与切换成本。
pages.counterexample: 开放性较低的人仍可以发明实用办法、喜欢小说、前往陌生地方，也可以在理由充分后带领重大变更。偏好经过验证的方法，不等于缺乏好奇、想象、勇气或学习能力。
pages.context_variation: 当新方案解决一个反复出现的具体问题、由可信的人演示，或第一次试验可以撤回时，探索更可能出现；当术语过于抽象、实施成本被隐藏，或可靠系统在没有明确收益时被打断，探索门槛会提高。
pages.combination_effects: 与较高尽责性组合时，这个区间可能支持细致标准化和稳定交付；与较低尽责性组合时，熟悉做法可能被保留，却没有持续维护。较高宜人性会让变更顾虑表达得更合作，较低宜人性则可能让质疑更直接、更集中于证据。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是保护连续性、看见落地成本，并把宽泛提案转成具体要求；潜在代价是过早折损陌生想法、过度依赖过去成功，或等待决策本身无法提供的确定性。合理平衡取决于可撤回程度与后果。
pages.communication_action: 面对新方法，先问清基线问题、一个可观察的成功指标、切换成本和回退点。当四项足够明确时同意有限试验，这样既保留有用的谨慎，也不必立即全盘采用或永久拒绝。
pages.not_meaning: 它不代表智力较低、创意较少、心胸狭窄、道德较差、无法学习、反对所有变化或只能做重复工作。它不是医疗诊断、能力判断、招聘筛选或成就预测。
pages.method_boundary: 区间标签压缩了连续自评分数，也可能遮住侧面层面的好奇、文化期待、接触新事物的机会和当前压力。解释时要比较重复选择和反例，不能把标签当成固定限制。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持层级特质模型，不支持缺陷语言或个人能力结论。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 群体变化模式不保证某个个人一定改变或保持稳定。

pages.title: High openness decision protocol: turn many ideas into one test
pages.summary: Use this legacy canonical as a practical protocol for managing an abundant idea portfolio: frame the decision, compare options, stop searching, and preserve learning without reopening the choice.
pages.meaning: The useful reader task here is not deciding whether high openness is good. It is converting broad exploration into a decision that can survive execution. The protocol assumes ideas are plentiful and asks which option best answers the current question under real constraints.
pages.possible_patterns: An idea portfolio may contain different solutions, different problem definitions, and attractive tangents that do not answer the decision. Without separation, comparison becomes unfair: a vivid possibility competes with a concrete plan, and each new thought resets the criteria.
pages.counterexample: More options do not always improve a high-openness decision. When the baseline already meets the requirement or the next experiment cannot change the choice, continued ideation adds delay rather than insight. Closing a search can be an expression of judgment, not a loss of curiosity.
pages.context_variation: Use a wider portfolio early, when the decision is reversible and the problem is uncertain. Narrow it faster when dependencies are waiting, evidence is converging, or implementation feedback will teach more than another concept discussion. Reopen only when a predeclared trigger appears.
pages.combination_effects: Higher conscientiousness can supply comparison criteria and execution checkpoints; lower conscientiousness may require an external owner for closure. Higher agreeableness may keep weak options alive to protect contributors, while lower agreeableness may discard them too quickly without preserving useful evidence.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: The protocol uses breadth, reframing, and connection-making while limiting restart cost and coordination ambiguity. Its tradeoff is that a stopping rule can close too early if the question or constraints were poorly framed, so one explicit dissent check belongs before commitment.
pages.communication_action: Write the decision in one sentence, classify each idea as answer, reframing, or tangent, score at most three answers against shared criteria, and name the stopping rule. Archive rejected ideas with the evidence that would justify reopening instead of keeping every option socially alive.
pages.not_meaning: This protocol does not prove a high score, superior creativity, innovation talent, leadership potential, or job fit. It does not replace the V2 range explanation, change the legacy canonical, or authorize a redirect; it is a bounded workflow for one reader task.
pages.method_boundary: A practical protocol is editorial guidance, not a validated treatment or prediction. Adapt it to consequence and team governance, and keep the underlying range result subject to the same self-report, facet, context, and individual-validity limitations as any other trait interpretation.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Provides trait-model context; it does not validate this editorial decision protocol.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Group-level research does not predict the outcome of this workflow for an individual.

pages.title: Low openness change worksheet: test a proposal without losing the baseline
pages.summary: Use this legacy canonical to evaluate change without framing caution as resistance: document the working baseline, set an evidence threshold, run a reversible trial, and compare outcomes.
pages.meaning: The reader task is to make a stability-first decision inspectable. Instead of arguing about being open or closed to change, the worksheet names what the current method protects, what problem the proposal solves, and what evidence would justify paying the switching cost.
pages.possible_patterns: A cautious reviewer may know operational details that a proposal omits, while a change advocate may see a recurring cost that familiarity has normalized. If neither side writes the baseline and threshold, the discussion collapses into identity language rather than a testable comparison.
pages.counterexample: Keeping the baseline is not automatically prudent. If failure repeats, the old method no longer meets the requirement, or a small trial is cheap and reversible, refusing to test can create more risk than controlled change. Stability must earn its place through evidence too.
pages.context_variation: Raise the evidence threshold for irreversible, regulated, safety-critical, or highly coordinated changes. Lower it for isolated trials with clear rollback, short feedback cycles, and limited downside. The threshold should follow consequence, not the status of the person proposing the idea.
pages.combination_effects: Higher conscientiousness may produce careful baselines and trial logs; lower conscientiousness may turn familiarity into passive drift. Higher neuroticism can amplify worst-case attention and improve risk discovery, but it may also require an explicit stop condition so threat scanning does not prevent learning.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: The worksheet preserves continuity, operational memory, and implementation realism while creating a legitimate path for evidence-based change. Its tradeoff is measurement overhead and the risk of choosing a threshold so demanding that no practical experiment could ever pass it.
pages.communication_action: Record the baseline outcome, the proposal's claimed improvement, one success metric, one unacceptable downside, trial duration, rollback owner, and decision date. After the trial, compare both options with the same evidence standard and document why the threshold was or was not met.
pages.not_meaning: This worksheet does not prove a low score, lack of creativity, resistance, poor learning ability, or preference for every routine. It does not replace the V2 low-range explanation, alter the canonical graph, or authorize publication, screening, diagnosis, or performance prediction.
pages.method_boundary: This is editorial decision support, not a psychometric intervention or guarantee of better choices. Results depend on metric quality, incentives, consequence, and execution; the underlying personality label remains a bounded self-report hypothesis rather than a fixed cause.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Provides trait-model context; it does not validate this editorial adoption worksheet.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Group-level evidence does not guarantee that a trial or one person's trait result will change.
